name: EMW R3/55
hook: In 1955 a racing car from a state-owned East German factory won its class at the Nürburgring, ahead of a Porsche.
story: Picture Eisenach after the war. The old car works sits in the Soviet zone. Money is short. Parts are short. The factory is now EMW, owned by the state. And a small racing team there decides to take on Porsche. Their car is the R3/55. A tiny six-cylinder, just a litre and a half. A light aluminium body over a frame of thin tubes. In May 1955 they bring it to the Eifel race at the Nürburgring. That is West German ground. Porsche is the favourite in the small sports cars. Then Richard von Frankenberg's Porsche spins off on some oil. Edgar Barth does not. He wins the class over ten laps. His teammate Paul Thiel is second. The best Porsche is only third. It does not last. The team is shut down in 1957. And Barth? He leaves the East that year, and goes to drive for Porsche.
description: The R3/55 was a sports racing car built by the racing collective of EMW, the state-owned works at Eisenach in East Germany, later renamed AWE. It used a 1.5-litre six-cylinder engine in a tubular trellis frame with an aluminium body. Driven by Edgar Barth, Paul Thiel and Arthur Rosenhammer, it raced Porsche and Borgward at the Nürburgring in 1955 and 1956. Racing development at Eisenach stopped after 1956. One car survives in the Automobile Welt Eisenach museum.
